title: Stargardt Disease: The Comprehensive Clinical Atlas
summary: Stargardt Disease (STGD1) is the most common hereditary juvenile macular dystrophy, characterized by progressive central vision loss driven by ABCA4-mediated toxic lipofuscin accumulation. This guide serves as a high-yield reference for the diagnosis, monitoring, and emerging therapeutic landscape of ABCA4-retinopathy.

sections.title: Definition & Molecular Pathogenesis
sections.content: Stargardt Disease (STGD1) is an autosomal recessive retinal dystrophy caused by mutations in the ABCA4 gene. The ABCA4 protein is an ATP-binding cassette transporter located on the disc membranes of rod and cone outer segments. Failure of this transporter leads to the accumulation of N-retinylidene-phosphatidylethanolamine (N-retinylidene-PE), which spontaneously condenses into toxic A2E (a major component of lipofuscin) within the Retinal Pigment Epithelium (RPE), leading to secondary photoreceptor death.

rows: Yellow-white sub-RPE deposits at the posterior pole
RPE atrophy centered at the fovea
A hallmark of FFA showing choroidal masking by RPE lipofuscin
Preservation of central vision in some advanced cases

sections.title: Red Flags: When to refer/suspect
content: Rapid vision loss in a teenager
Presence of pisciform yellow flecks beyond the arcades

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup Sequence
content: Step 1: BCVA and Color Vision (Ishihara/HRR) testing.
Step 2: Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF) - essential for visualizing hypo/hyper-autofluorescent flecks.
Step 3: Fundus Fluorescein Angiography (FFA) - Classic 'Dark Choroid' sign.
Step 4: SD-OCT - Quantifying ellipsoid zone (EZ) loss and outer retinal atrophy.
Step 5: ERG/EOG - To assess global rod/cone function.
Step 6: Molecular genetic testing (ABCA4 gene panel).

content.explanation: S: Symmetric atrophy; T: Toxic lipofuscin accumulation; G: Genetic (ABCA4); D: Dark choroid on FFA.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: The 'Dark Choroid' occurs because lipofuscin in the RPE absorbs the background choroidal fluorescence.
Avoid high-dose Vitamin A supplementation, which may accelerate lipofuscin accumulation.
Recent advances focus on gene therapy (AAV-mediated) and sub-retinal transplantation.
Prognosis is generally favorable for central vision until the atrophy involves the foveal center.
